\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة} (fī tilka al-layla)}{في تلك الليلة (fī tilka al-layla)}]{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة} (fī tilka al-layla) — that night}

\label{lesson:AR-C327-fi-tilka-al-layla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an arrow, then the Arabic for armour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة}}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة}} — \emph{fī tilka al-layla} — \textquotedblleft{}that night\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة} \ar{لم} \ar{ينم} \ar{أحد} \ar{في} \ar{البيت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fī tilka al-layla lam yanam aḥad fī al-bayt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That night nobody in the house slept.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة}} (\emph{fī tilka al-layla}) is \textquotedblleft{}in that night\textquotedblright{}: \emph{layla}, one night, is built on the inherited Semitic root \emph{l-y-l} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{layl}; EtymDB sets it beside Hebrew \emph{laylā} and Aramaic \emph{lēlyā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī tilka al-layla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī tilka al-layla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī tilka al-layla lam yanam aḥad fī al-bayt.} — That night nobody in the house slept.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an arrow, then the Arabic for armour, then say \emph{fī tilka al-layla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}That night\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه} (fī al-waqt nafsih)}{في الوقت نفسه (fī al-waqt nafsih)}]{\ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه} (fī al-waqt nafsih) — at the same time}

\label{lesson:AR-C327-fi-al-waqt-nafsih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for armour, then the Arabic for that night.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه}}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه}} — \emph{fī al-waqt nafsih} — \textquotedblleft{}at the same time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تطبخ} \ar{أمي} \ar{وتتكلم} \ar{في} \ar{الهاتف} \ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taṭbukhu ummī wa-tatakallamu fī al-hātif fī al-waqt nafsih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother cooks and talks on the phone at the same time.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه}} (\emph{fī al-waqt nafsih}) is \textquotedblleft{}in the time itself\textquotedblright{}: \emph{waqt} is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-q-t} (Lane), and \emph{nafs}, \textquotedblleft{}self, soul\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{n-f-s}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-waqt nafsih}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-waqt nafsih}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭbukhu ummī wa-tatakallamu fī al-hātif fī al-waqt nafsih.} — My mother cooks and talks on the phone at the same time.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for armour, then the Arabic for that night, then say \emph{fī al-waqt nafsih} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حالما} (ḥālamā)}{حالما (ḥālamā)}]{\ar{حالما} (ḥālamā) — as soon as}

\label{lesson:AR-C327-halama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for that night, then the Arabic for at the same time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حالما}}
\textbf{\ar{حالما}} — \emph{ḥālamā} — \textquotedblleft{}as soon as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حالما} \ar{وصلت} \ar{اتصلت} \ar{بأمي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥālamā waṣaltu ittaṣaltu bi-ummī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
As soon as I arrived I called my mother.
\end{quote}

A past verb follows it in a story.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حالما}} (\emph{ḥālamā}) is built on \emph{ḥāl}, \textquotedblleft{}a state, the present moment\textquotedblright{}, from the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-l} (Lane), with \emph{mā}: \textquotedblleft{}in the moment that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥālamā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥālamā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥālamā waṣaltu ittaṣaltu bi-ummī.} — As soon as I arrived I called my mother.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for that night, then the Arabic for at the same time, then say \emph{ḥālamā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حالما} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}As soon as\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إلى} \ar{أن} (ilā an)}{إلى أن (ilā an)}]{\ar{إلى} \ar{أن} (ilā an) — until}

\label{lesson:AR-C327-ila-an}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for at the same time, then the Arabic for as soon as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إلى} \ar{أن}}
\textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{أن}} — \emph{ilā an} — \textquotedblleft{}until\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتظرنا} \ar{إلى} \ar{أن} \ar{توقف} \ar{المطر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intaẓarnā ilā an tawaqqafa al-maṭar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We waited until the rain stopped.
\end{quote}

A verb follows: \ar{إلى} \ar{أن} \ar{وصل}. Before a noun, say \ar{حتى}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{أن}} (\emph{ilā an}) joins the preposition \emph{ilā}, \textquotedblleft{}to, as far as\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{an}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}up to the time that\textquotedblright{}. Lane treats both as old particles; their origin beyond Arabic is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ilā an}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ilā an}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intaẓarnā ilā an tawaqqafa al-maṭar.} — We waited until the rain stopped.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for at the same time, then the Arabic for as soon as, then say \emph{ilā an} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إلى} \ar{أن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Until\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طوال} (ṭuwāla)}{طوال (ṭuwāla)}]{\ar{طوال} (ṭuwāla) — throughout, all through}

\label{lesson:AR-C327-tuwala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for as soon as, then the Arabic for until.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طوال}}
\textbf{\ar{طوال}} — \emph{ṭuwāla} — \textquotedblleft{}throughout, all through\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بقي} \ar{المريض} \ar{في} \ar{السرير} \ar{طوال} \ar{الأسبوع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baqiya al-marīḍ fī as-sarīr ṭuwāla al-usbūʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The patient stayed in bed all week.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طوال}} (\emph{ṭuwāla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-w-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to be long\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{ṭawīl}. \emph{Ṭuwāla} is \textquotedblleft{}for the length of\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭuwāla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭuwāla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baqiya al-marīḍ fī as-sarīr ṭuwāla al-usbūʿ.} — The patient stayed in bed all week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for as soon as, then the Arabic for until, then say \emph{ṭuwāla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{طوال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Throughout, all through\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
